scope: Qualified OMP 18.0.9 macOS arm64, Windows x64, and Linux x64 clients; the digest-pinned RTX 5090 runtime image a62dd5b8 under deployment profile qwen38-5090-v0.6.3 (configuration 622ab621); the RTX 4090 native package v0.6.1-beta.1; the RTX 3090 durable v0.2.5-beta.1 package. No component, profile or configuration changed from v0.6.3. This release changes the config a route installs beside the client: the pinned client no longer advertises an out-of-channel `omp update` (#18). Measured on 2026-09-12 (EXP-034) by re-running every client-installing route from its own blocks and reading the setting back from the installed client.

local_release_packaging.build_route_note: built by the appliance's canonical route (pinned runpod/pytorch:1.1.0-cu1300-torch291-ubuntu2404 container on the owner appliance, clean tree d956e6d6, 9/9 host suites plus the io_uring checkpoint backend suite); the runtime image was built from the published release binaries by the publish-runtime-image workflow (run 34225710385) and its receipt is attached to the runtime-image release

rtx5090.lifecycle: candidate and published-image runs both started and stopped through tools/lifecycle/ninfer_container.py (preflight bound image id, binary, model artifact, and configuration identity); the configuration identity computed from the published image equals the qualified one, so the profile did not drift between qualification and publication
rtx5090.fanout_branch_reuse: private_long_anchor (4/4 branches at 57,853 and 67,717 tokens in one process, and 4/4 again after a verified restart at each size)
rtx5090.post_restart_branch_reuse: private_long_anchor (8/8 across both sizes; no root re-prefill)
rtx5090.warm_arrival: both orders hot after a verified restart: resume-first 4.386 s resume then forks at 2.876 s and 1.353 s, fork-first likewise hot; every resume quoted the planted keys exactly
rtx5090.agent_protocol: fork/delete/no-resurrection across docker restart passed on the published image and on the candidate
rtx5090.origin_authentication: inherited from v0.4.7 (store format unchanged; the lifecycle candidate loaded MAC-tagged generations from a fresh store)
rtx5090.measured_on: published image a62dd5b8 for retrieval, decode, agent protocol, identity, auth boundary and completion; the appliance-built image of the same bytes for fanout, warm arrival and restore

rtx4090_windows_native.protocol_checks: 15/15 at the shipped pool and 15/15 at 8 host state slots
rtx4090_windows_native.rollback: bidirectional; candidate stopped by signal, predecessor by what its record declares

rtx3090_windows_native.carried_from: v0.5.0 (component byte-identical; requalified on its own rig on 2026-09-05 with origin-authenticated checkpoints)

interpretation: All three documented routes that install an OMP client config pass end to end at the candidate, and each one's installed client reports `startup.checkUpdate` false: macOS 10/10 from an isolated HOME, the native Windows client 5/5, the RTX 4090 native route 7/7.

The pinned 18.0.9 client reads the setting only in nested form; a dotted `startup.checkUpdate:` key leaves the default true. The shipped config uses the nested form and a test refuses any other shape.
Every route's fail-closed check still fails the outage request, so the config change did not weaken the boundary it is installed next to.

Two runner defects found on the way are fixed with regression tests: the route refused nothing when a stale forward owned its port (a false green followed by a false fail-closed), and a failed run left its forward listening.
Component bytes, profiles, configuration, and the OMP client are unchanged and carry their receipts by hash.
This release's evidence carries a correction of record: v0.6.5's receipts claimed the appliance's production lane had been restored when it had not. No v0.6.5 measurement is affected; the claim was.
Raw prompts, model outputs, private host identifiers, and raw request logs are excluded.
